encounters.summary: Added the pure §6 encounter rules as @pirate-sea-race/simulation/encounters (geometry.ts: supercover LOS, bearing by max dot product, circular cones, squared ranges; modes.ts: full sea rules + foot placeholder; state.ts: config/state/events/markers; step.ts: stepEncounters/replayEncounters) and the tuning as @pirate-sea-race/content/encounters (constants in seconds converted to ticks, zod validator). One subpath export added to each of packages/simulation/package.json and packages/content/package.json (source condition first); no postbuild, dependency, barrel or tsconfig changed. Tests: content validator test (negative duration, range above sight radius), geometry tests (supercover equals an exact rational reference on all 6561 pairs of a 9x9 grid, both directions; land blocks, shoals do not; ±4/±8 cone boundaries; exact squared-range boundary), 43 scripted rule tests, and seeded property tests over the slice sea and three synthetic maps (40 seeds x 1600 ticks: invariants every tick, replay hash equality, EXERCISED coverage of every event kind and reason, input reorder and two order-preserving relabellings). docs/encounters.md written. Executed locally after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run test:unit (684 passed), npm run test:integration (37 passed), npm run build (exit 0, smoke passed); also imported both new subpaths from dist/ by hand.
open_assumptions: A defender who becomes ineligible during the windup (e.g. reserved by someone else's hit on an earlier tick) makes the attempt a miss with cooldown, following §6/the task literally; only same-tick losses are preemptions.
An attacker who disconnects, leaves the snapshot, changes mode or is reserved during the windup has the attempt cancelled (no cooldown).
End reports are also accepted while a duel is still in transition (quit or server fault before the fight starts).
Protection and respawn durations count from the ticks named in the reports (settlement tick, fight end tick), not from the tick the report arrives.
Duel markers carry only {x, y, startTick} with startTick = reservation tick; no duel id because the id contains player ids.
The encounter position is the floor midpoint of the two players at the hit; respawn opponents are every other snapshot player not respawning (disconnected and dueling players included).
If no pair of draw points exists within 6 tiles, both ships stay where they were (documented fallback).
scripts/smoke-build.ts does not yet load the two new subpaths (per decisions.md the assistant adds them at merge).

findings.message: packages/simulation/src/encounters/step.ts: players freed within a tick (settlement returns in step 2 via settle(), respawns in step 3) are immediately eligible attackers in step 6 of the same tick, but the snapshot still holds their pre-return position (the caller only moves them after reading player-returned/player-respawned). A loser pressing on the respawn tick therefore picks a target (range, cone, line of sight) from the old encounter location, loses the 20 s respawn protection, and gets an attempt-started naming a player near a place they no longer are; the attempt then almost surely misses at landing and costs the 6 s cooldown. Draw/win returns have the same one-tick window. Neither the code nor docs/encounters.md tells the caller to suppress presses on that tick; skipping attack presses for players returned or respawned on the current tick would close it.
findings.requirement: Positions come from the snapshot; the rules never move ships.

This is documented as an open assumption. It is harmless but differs from a literal 'elapsed time' of the duel.

Because the loser's respawn counts from end.tick, a caller bug reporting an early end tick shortens the respawn wait instead of being refused as 'invalid'.
findings.requirement: For a fight that ran, the caller reports its end: `win` (winner), `draw`, or `cancelled` (a server fault or double forfeit), with the tick it ended.

findings.message: packages/simulation/src/encounters/modes.ts seaModeRules.separateReturn: when no pair of navigable tiles within 6 tiles is at least 3 apart, both ships are left where they were, which breaks the separation rule (documented fallback, unlikely on the slice sea). Candidates also ignore sea connectivity, so on a map with shoal walls (for example the slice sea's column-55 reef) a draw could in principle place a ship on the other side of a barrier. The minimum-cost pairing makes that rare but does not rule it out.
findings.requirement: A draw or cancellation returns both players to two distinct navigable points near the encounter position, at least 3 tiles apart and within 6 tiles, with 8 s of protection.

findings.message: Foot-mode cooldown and cone are only partly tested. In packages/simulation/src/encounters/encounters.test.ts:598-599, the step meant to show the six-second foot cooldown refusing presses calls world.runTo(133), which never presses. So `attempt-started` is always empty and the assertion passes whether or not the cooldown is enforced. Only the cooldownEndTick value (134) is really checked. The test at :602 is named "hits within ±4 of the aim and picks targets in the ±8 front cone", but it only checks a target directly behind against one straight ahead. It never exercises the ±4 hit boundary or the ±8 target boundary in foot mode. The ship-mode tests (encounters.test.ts:114, :184, :202, :212) and geometry.test.ts:152 cover the shared code, so this is minor.
findings.requirement: For foot mode, test only timing, range, cone and cooldown.

findings.message: Two dock-choice tie-breaks are untested. modes.ts:90-99 breaks ties by dock iteration order (`key < chosen.key`, `key > chosen.key`), but no scripted or property test sets up two clear docks at equal distance from the encounter, or two fallback docks with equal nearest-opponent distance. The tests at encounters.test.ts:466 and :484 cover the nearest clear dock, skipping a watched dock and the farthest fallback, but none of them has a tie. The seeded properties only check that respawn points are navigable and carry a dock id.
findings.requirement: The spawn is at a dock chosen deterministically: the dock nearest the encounter with no other active player within `SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES`, ties by dock id; if none qualifies, the dock farthest from its nearest opponent.

inputs.decisions:
# Decisions: encounters-core

From the overnight session of 2026-09-24. The operator is asleep and asked the assistant to decide, record each decision, and use the workflow for the code.

## Decisions

- Slice 4 (`encounters-theft`) is split in two. This feature holds the pure §6 rules, like `claim-channel` and `objectives-ledger` did. `encounters-online` then wires them, the ledger and the duel into `MatchRoom`. Pure rules can be proven exhaustively (symmetry, seeded properties) before any network is involved, and they can run in parallel with `sea-compact-fixes`.
- It's based on sea-compact-001's approved candidate (`8328920`), so tests on the slice sea use the compact map that will ship.
- Where the duel runs: in the encounters slice, the duel moves into `MatchRoom` as a simulation object (§14). The standalone `DuelRoom` stays as the practice arena. This feature only emits events for it.
- Values the spec leaves open, all as content constants to tune after playtests:
  - the grapple range is `ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES` (6); the island challenge range is 2 tiles;
  - the hit area is ±4 headings (±22.5°) around the aim locked at the start; target choice uses a ±8-heading (±45°) front cone;
  - the grapple miss cooldown is 6 s, the same as §6's challenge miss;
  - land blocks line of sight and shoals don't (ships see over reefs).
- The rules pick the target (nearest eligible, then lowest id) rather than the client, so a client can't aim at a hidden player (§16).
- A press with no eligible target starts nothing and costs nothing. That's forgiving for players and gives no information away. Only a real miss costs the cooldown.
- A hit that loses a same-tick conflict is "preempted" and costs no cooldown, because the attacker didn't miss.
- Readiness: the duel starts after the 3 s countdown once both clients are ready. One client not ready at 10 s forfeits; both not ready at 10 s cancels (§12's same-tick double forfeit).
- Return timing: the world return happens at ledger settlement (after the theft choice), but the loser's 15 s respawn counts from the fight's end, so the choice window doesn't lengthen it.
- The loser's respawn dock is the nearest one with no opponent within sight, falling back to the farthest from any opponent. It's deterministic and hard to camp.

- Corrected after design challenge attempt 1:
  - Line of sight and returns are per-mode. Ships are fully specified, and on foot is a placeholder until walking exists (land can't block the sight of players standing on it).
  - The geometry is defined once: a supercover line, the bearing by maximal dot product (ties low), ±N as circular difference, distance 0 inside.
  - A hit refused by the cap is a preemption (no cooldown); duels count until settlement.
  - A readiness forfeit ends the duel inside the encounter state, and the caller only reports its settlement.
  - Protection ended by a claim or collection reaches the encounter step one tick later (§5 order); that 50 ms lag is accepted.

## Assumptions

- Only ships exist in the world today. The island challenge is built and tested with caller-supplied on-foot positions, ready for when walking on islands lands in `objectives-endgame`.
- With eight players at most, four duels is also the natural limit. The cap is enforced anyway, as §14 states it.
- The assistant adds the new subpaths to `scripts/smoke-build.ts` at merge, as for `claim-channel`.

## Deferred

- Wiring into `MatchRoom`, the arena transition UI, the world duel marker and the theft-choice UI: `encounters-online`.
- Walking on islands: `objectives-endgame`.
- Tuning the ranges, cones and cooldowns after the first playtest of encounters.

concerns.message: The attempt resolves on eligibility at landing, and a failed landing is 'attempt-missed' with a cooldown. So if a third party's hit reserves the defender one tick before this attempt lands, the attacker pays the 6 s miss cooldown. If the two hits land on the same tick, the second is 'preempted' at no cost. decisions.md says only a real miss should cost the cooldown ('the attacker didn't miss'). A defender who is reserved (or starts respawning) during the windup did not escape.
concerns.consequence: Two identical situations one tick apart get opposite penalties, and the scripted and property tests will lock in the unfair version. Fixing it later means changing tests and events in encounters-online. Recommendation: when the defender becomes reserved or ineligible for a reason other than moving, cancel or preempt the attempt at that tick with no cooldown. Keep 'missed' for range, cone and line of sight only.

concerns.message: End reports are described only 'for a fight that ran'. The ledger can resolve a duel before the fight starts: during the 3 to 10 s transition, an explicit quit makes the ledger forfeit that player at once (the recordResult forfeit path in objectives/duels.ts), and a server fault can also end the duel early. If the encounter state refuses end reports during the transition, it keeps counting down. At 10 s it emits its own readiness forfeit, or a cancel, which can contradict the ledger's win, and its end tick is wrong by up to 10 s.
concerns.consequence: The loser's 15 s respawn is timed from the wrong tick, a duel can be ended twice with different outcomes, and the settlement report may reach a duel the encounter still thinks is in transition. Recommendation: accept an end report in both the transition and running phases, and let it stop the readiness timer. Add one scripted test for a quit during the countdown.

concerns.message: Draw and cancel returns ask for two distinct navigable points at least 3 tiles apart and within 6 tiles. Four things are missing. (1) Which 'encounter position' to use when the two players stood at different points. (2) A fallback when no such pair exists: narrow channels, or small synthetic maps in the property test. (3) Reachability: seaValidation only checks that docks and spawn slots are reachable, not every navigable tile, so a point across a thin island strip or in an enclosed pocket passes 'navigable'. (4) What happens when a point is taken by another ship.
concerns.consequence: On a synthetic map the property test either fails or the worker adds an unreviewed fallback. In live play a ship can be put on the far side of land or stuck in an unreachable pocket. Recommendation: search outward (breadth-first) from the encounter tile over navigable tiles within 6 tiles, which guarantees the points are connected by sea. Pick the pair deterministically, and document a fallback (for example, the best pair found, otherwise both at the encounter tile).

concerns.message: The hit area at landing is 'within range and within ±4 headings of the aim locked at the start', but it doesn't say where the cone starts: at the attacker's position at the start of the attempt, or where the attacker is at landing. With a locked aim and a moving start point, the attacker can partly steer the grapple during the windup by sailing sideways.
concerns.consequence: Whichever reading the worker picks becomes documented rules and tests. It sets how easy escape is, which is the fairness core of §6, and changing it later is rework. Settle it in docs/encounters.md: I recommend the positions of both players at landing, since the snapshot holds only current positions.

concerns.message: The encounter state tracks its own copy of each duel's lifecycle (reserved, transition, running, ended, settled). The ledger already tracks the same thing (fighting, choosing, settled), and the caller must keep the two in sync with separate end and settlement reports. The cap rule ('counts until settlement'), refused second end reports, and forfeits inside the encounter state all come from keeping two sources of truth.
concerns.consequence: The two states can drift apart, for example on the quit-in-transition path above, or when the ledger refuses a report the encounter already accepted. That produces cap miscounts or ghost duels that encounters-online must debug over the network. The worker should add a property check that every reservation event is followed by exactly one end and one settlement before release.

concerns.message: sea-compact-fixes runs at the same time and owns the sea, the sailing constants and possibly heading.ts and the slice sea map. Scripted encounter tests that hard-code coordinates or literal ranges on the slice sea will break when that feature changes the map or ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES / SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES.
concerns.consequence: Failures appear at merge and are hard to attribute. Keep scripted geometry tests on small synthetic maps. Slice-sea property tests should sample positions from the map's navigable tiles and docks, and every range should come from the imported constants.

concerns.message: The loser's respawn dock rule doesn't say when the dock is chosen: at settlement, when the loser returns, or at the respawn tick 15 s after the fight ended. It also doesn't say who counts as an 'other active player': players in a duel (shown as a marker), respawning players, disconnected players.
concerns.consequence: Choosing at settlement uses opponent positions up to about 10 s old, so the dock can be camped by the time the loser appears, which undermines the anti-camping reason in decisions.md. Recommendation: choose at the respawn tick, counting only players who are in the world and in ship mode. Document it and test it.

concerns.message: The scope is large for one lane with a two-hour stop rule. It covers two modes, integer geometry, attempts and same-tick resolution, the readiness transition, duel bookkeeping, three return rules, protection, match end, symmetry and seeded property tests with EXERCISED coverage, the content zod schema, docs and two subpath exports.
concerns.consequence: There is a real chance the lane reports 'blocked' after two hours with property or coverage tests failing, or ships with thin return and transition tests. Build the geometry and attempt/resolution core with its tests first, so any partial result is still useful.

challenge.simpler_alternative: Keep the encounter state to what only it knows: attempts, cooldowns, protection, the readiness countdown and respawn timers. Take 'in or reserved for a duel' and the unresolved-duel count from the snapshot, which the caller derives from the ledger. Also count hits accepted earlier in the same step, so the four-duel cap holds within one tick. This removes the second duel lifecycle, the separate end-then-settlement reports, the refused second end, and the risk of the two states drifting apart. Return placement (the winner's position, the loser's dock, the two draw points) becomes pure helper functions that the caller runs when the ledger settles the duel, tested on their own. This keeps every rule in the task. It only moves where the duel state lives, and it matches the ledger as the single writer for duel outcomes (§14).
challenge.cheap_experiment: Before coding, write a 30-line throwaway script on the compact slice sea. (a) For every navigable tile, check whether a breadth-first search over navigable tiles within 6 tiles finds two tiles at least 3 apart, and whether every navigable tile is reachable by sea from spawn slot 0. (b) Tabulate grapple landings with the ±4 cone and 1 s windup: defender at 1 to 6 tiles, stationary or at full speed with each of the 64 headings, starting from standstill or already at speed (39 sub-units per step, acceleration 3), measuring the cone from the attacker's position at landing. If (a) finds pockets or tiles with no valid pair, the draw rule must switch to a sea-connected search with a fallback. If (b) shows grapples almost never land except on stationary or tail-chased ships, the hit-area rule (cone start, ±4 width) should be settled now rather than after playtests, because the tests will lock it in.

encounters.task:
# Task: encounters

## Goal

Build the encounter rules of §6 as pure, deterministic code: who can attack whom, the telegraphed attempt and its escape, same-tick reservation, the ready-checked transition into a duel, and the return to the world with protection. | | Sea grapple (ship → ship) | Island challenge (on foot → on foot) |
|---|---|---|
| Windup, telegraphed | 1 s | 0.6 s lunge |
| Range | `ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES` (6) | 2 tiles |

A hit that loses to an earlier one is `attempt-preempted`, with no cooldown. The order players or attempts appear in the input never matters.
- **Reservation and transition.** A hit reserves both players as a duel with a stable id derived from the tick and the two ids. The transition shows a 3 s countdown. The duel starts when the countdown is over and both players are ready (the snapshot reports readiness). A player not ready 10 s after the reservation forfeits. If both are still not ready at 10 s, the duel is cancelled (both forfeit on the same tick, §12). A readiness forfeit or cancel ends the duel in the encounter state itself, with that tick as its end tick, and emits an event the caller hands to the ledger. The caller then reports only its settlement, never a second end.
- **The duel.** While a duel runs, its players are in it. The state exposes a marker per duel for other players: position and start tick for the elapsed time, and nothing else. For a fight that ran, the caller reports its end: `win` (winner), `draw`, or `cancelled` (a server fault or double forfeit), with the tick it ended. Separately, it reports the tick the ledger settled it (after the theft choice). A second end report for the same duel is refused and changes nothing.
- **Return** (§6), at settlement:
  - The winner returns at their encounter position with 8 s of protection.
  - The loser respawns 15 s after the fight ended (not after settlement), with 20 s of protection. The spawn is at a dock chosen deterministically: the dock nearest the encounter with no other active player within `SIGHT_RADIUS_TILES`, ties by dock id; if none qualifies, the dock farthest from its nearest opponent.
  - A draw or cancellation returns both players to two distinct navigable points near the encounter position, at least 3 tiles apart and within 6 tiles, with 8 s of protection.
- **Protection** has a source (`spawn`, `win`, `draw`, `respawn`) and an end tick. It ends early when the protected player starts an attempt, or when the snapshot reports that the claim or ledger ended their protection. Because §5 runs encounters before claims, the caller passes the **previous** tick's claim and ledger results. The one-tick (50 ms) lag is accepted and documented. The caller gives spawn protection at match start through the config or state.
- **Match end.** A duel still running at the deadline ends without theft (the claim code emits that event). This step only needs a way for the caller to cancel every attempt and stop new ones once the match is over.

# Decisions: encounters-core

## Decisions

- Slice 4 (`encounters-theft`) is split in two. This feature holds the pure §6 rules, like `claim-channel` and `objectives-ledger` did. `encounters-online` then wires them, the ledger and the duel into `MatchRoom`. Pure rules can be proven exhaustively (symmetry, seeded properties) before any network is involved, and they can run in parallel with `sea-compact-fixes`.
- It's based on sea-compact-001's approved candidate (`8328920`), so tests on the slice sea use the compact map that will ship.
- Where the duel runs: in the encounters slice, the duel moves into `MatchRoom` as a simulation object (§14). The standalone `DuelRoom` stays as the practice arena. This feature only emits events for it.
- Values the spec leaves open, all as content constants to tune after playtests:
  - the grapple range is `ENGAGEMENT_RANGE_TILES` (6); the island challenge range is 2 tiles;
  - the hit area is ±4 headings (±22.5°) around the aim locked at the start; target choice uses a ±8-heading (±45°) front cone;
  - the grapple miss cooldown is 6 s, the same as §6's challenge miss;
  - land blocks line of sight and shoals don't (ships see over reefs).
- The rules pick the target (nearest eligible, then lowest id) rather than the client, so a client can't aim at a hidden player (§16).
- A press with no eligible target starts nothing and costs nothing. That's forgiving for players and gives no information away. Only a real miss costs the cooldown.
- A hit that loses a same-tick conflict is "preempted" and costs no cooldown, because the attacker didn't miss.
- Readiness: the duel starts after the 3 s countdown once both clients are ready. One client not ready at 10 s forfeits; both not ready at 10 s cancels (§12's same-tick double forfeit).
- Return timing: the world return happens at ledger settlement (after the theft choice), but the loser's 15 s respawn counts from the fight's end, so the choice window doesn't lengthen it.
- The loser's respawn dock is the nearest one with no opponent within sight, falling back to the farthest from any opponent. It's deterministic and hard to camp.

- Corrected after design challenge attempt 1:
  - Line of sight and returns are per-mode. Ships are fully specified, and on foot is a placeholder until walking exists (land can't block the sight of players standing on it).
  - The geometry is defined once: a supercover line, the bearing by maximal dot product (ties low), ±N as circular difference, distance 0 inside.
  - A hit refused by the cap is a preemption (no cooldown); duels count until settlement.
  - A readiness forfeit ends the duel inside the encounter state, and the caller only reports its settlement.
  - Protection ended by a claim or collection reaches the encounter step one tick later (§5 order); that 50 ms lag is accepted.

## Assumptions

- Only ships exist in the world today. The island challenge is built and tested with caller-supplied on-foot positions, ready for when walking on islands lands in `objectives-endgame`.
- With eight players at most, four duels is also the natural limit. The cap is enforced anyway, as §14 states it.
- The assistant adds the new subpaths to `scripts/smoke-build.ts` at merge, as for `claim-channel`.

- Wiring into `MatchRoom`, the arena transition UI, the world duel marker and the theft-choice UI: `encounters-online`.
- Walking on islands: `objectives-endgame`.
- Tuning the ranges, cones and cooldowns after the first playtest of encounters.

completion.summary: Added the pure §6 encounter rules as @pirate-sea-race/simulation/encounters (geometry.ts: supercover LOS, bearing by max dot product, circular cones, squared ranges; modes.ts: full sea rules + foot placeholder; state.ts: config/state/events/markers; step.ts: stepEncounters/replayEncounters) and the tuning as @pirate-sea-race/content/encounters (constants in seconds converted to ticks, zod validator). One subpath export added to each of packages/simulation/package.json and packages/content/package.json (source condition first); no postbuild, dependency, barrel or tsconfig changed. Tests: content validator test (negative duration, range above sight radius), geometry tests (supercover equals an exact rational reference on all 6561 pairs of a 9x9 grid, both directions; land blocks, shoals do not; ±4/±8 cone boundaries; exact squared-range boundary), 43 scripted rule tests, and seeded property tests over the slice sea and three synthetic maps (40 seeds x 1600 ticks: invariants every tick, replay hash equality, EXERCISED coverage of every event kind and reason, input reorder and two order-preserving relabellings). docs/encounters.md written. Executed locally after npm ci: npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run test:unit (684 passed), npm run test:integration (37 passed), npm run build (exit 0, smoke passed); also imported both new subpaths from dist/ by hand.
open_assumptions: A defender who becomes ineligible during the windup (e.g. reserved by someone else's hit on an earlier tick) makes the attempt a miss with cooldown, following §6/the task literally; only same-tick losses are preemptions.
An attacker who disconnects, leaves the snapshot, changes mode or is reserved during the windup has the attempt cancelled (no cooldown).
End reports are also accepted while a duel is still in transition (quit or server fault before the fight starts).
Protection and respawn durations count from the ticks named in the reports (settlement tick, fight end tick), not from the tick the report arrives.
Duel markers carry only {x, y, startTick} with startTick = reservation tick; no duel id because the id contains player ids.
The encounter position is the floor midpoint of the two players at the hit; respawn opponents are every other snapshot player not respawning (disconnected and dueling players included).
If no pair of draw points exists within 6 tiles, both ships stay where they were (documented fallback).
scripts/smoke-build.ts does not yet load the two new subpaths (per decisions.md the assistant adds them at merge).
